book_bed_ledger.title: The Bed Counter's Ledger
book_bed_ledger.author: an unnamed attendant before the Dawn
book_bed_ledger.text:
Twelve beds. Twelve clean blankets. Eleven cups.

Apprentice took a cup downstairs. Remind him tomorrow.

Twelve beds. Thirteen blankets. Someone expects company.

Instructions arrived from the Office. We are to keep everyone in their assigned places until the ceremony ends.

Twelve beds. Twelve blankets. No one sleeping.

Count again in the morning.

book_final_atlas.title: Instructions for the Final Atlas
book_final_atlas.author: the Unclosed Office, unsigned circular
book_final_atlas.text:
Each road shall receive a destination. Each settlement shall receive a place. Each border shall receive an owner.

Unregistered valleys must be reported before dawn. Reports received after dawn will be considered impossible and returned to their sender.

Please refrain from moving during the completion ceremony. The Office cannot accept responsibility for persons entered under the wrong country.

Tomorrow, the map will be finished.

book_handles.title: On the Ownership of Handles
book_handles.author: Pella of the Blue Handle
book_handles.text:
My first handle was chosen by the woman who made me. It was a good handle. I used it for thirty years.

When it broke, the mender asked what kind I wanted. Nobody had asked before.

I chose blue. My maker would have preferred green. I think we could have discussed it over tea.

I would have poured.

book_waiting_cup.title: A Cup for Whoever Comes Next
book_waiting_cup.author: a Hearthkeeper's household, copied anonymously
book_waiting_cup.text:
We used to set an extra place at supper for travelers. Then we had three travelers and only one spare plate. Grandmother said the custom needed improvement.

Now we keep a clean cup beside the door. Whoever comes next may use it. Whoever comes after that may wash it.

Grandmother called this hospitality. Grandfather called it a successful division of labor. They agreed for nearly sixty years.

book_warm_letter.title: A Letter Kept Warm
book_warm_letter.author: Iven, recipient unnamed
book_warm_letter.text:
I charged the scarf at the inn. It will keep its warmth until morning. There is a loose thread beside the clasp, so pull gently.

You said I never remember practical things. I remembered the scarf, the bread, and your terrible little spoon.

I meant to remember a better goodbye. You will have to accept this one until I return.

book_water_notes.title: Notes on Keeping Water
book_water_notes.author: caravan mender Sef Dapple
book_water_notes.text:
Shade the jar before you shade your boots. Boots complain less expensively.

Repair a crack before the journey. A cup repaired halfway across the wastes becomes a meeting of everybody's opinions.

I have seen a rain jar emptied by a careless child and by a very careful adult. The child admitted it sooner.

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: I miss my old crew most at mealtimes. Nobody here argues quite the same way.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: We argued over every meal on the road. I'd gladly hear it again.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: A quiet supper makes me remember my crew. We were never quiet over food.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: My companions found something to disagree about at every meal. I miss those voices.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: My old crew brought five flags and one cooking pot. We learned which one mattered when it rained.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: My crew carried five flags and a single cooking pot. Rain taught us which to worry about.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Five flags in our packs. One cooking pot. We kept the pot dry first.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: We brought five flags on the road and cooked in one pot. Bad weather made us practical.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Rain didn't care about our five flags. Supper depended on the one pot.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Our crew had five flags between us and one cooking pot. We all agreed about the pot when the rain came.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: A gate opening is a chance to leave as well as a chance to go deeper.

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Supper is being set out. No helmets at the table. That rule took my old crew years to learn.

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: They're setting supper. My crew needed years to learn that helmets weren't tableware.

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: The table is being laid. We can eat without armor getting a place of its own.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Supper is over. The cups are drying. Nobody argued about watch duty. I could get used to that.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Supper's over. A quiet meal with no watch-duty argument still surprises me.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: The cups are drying, and nobody has assigned me the late watch. Good evening.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: We've finished eating. I enjoyed hearing no quarrel about who stayed awake afterward.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: The meal ended pleasantly. Nobody tried to trade watch duty for the last serving.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: Supper's finished. A clean cup and no watch roster make a fine end to it.

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: I once found a dry place under a tower whose builders knew two moons. A good roof travels well between worlds.

lines.speaker: retired_delver
lines.text: The tower I slept under was built beneath a sky with two moons. Our rain still stayed outside.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: My grandmother said the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister said four. They argued until sunset.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Grandmother counted three days of Dawn. Her sister counted four. Neither would let the other have the last word.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Our family has two accounts of the Dawn: three days and four. Both are in the same book.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Grandmother insisted the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister added a fourth every time she told it.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Three days, Grandmother said. Four, said her sister. Their argument lasted longer than either account.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: I've copied both family accounts of the Dawn. If I choose three days or four, somebody's ghost will complain.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: A delivery is being sorted in the square. I offered to count the crates. They said I should count cups instead.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The delivery has been received. Those crates can wait a little while. Tired hands make poor knots.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The fountain offers rest. Keeping the steps clean is my contribution.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The water does its work. I do the sweeping.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Rest by the fountain. You needn't earn a place beside it.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: I tend the fountain and make sure there's room around it. Some days that means moving a very stubborn crate.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The fountain has heard more road stories than I have. I still like listening.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Some bells are waiting for people, too.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: A wrapped bell can wait a long time.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Some bells stay quiet until their traveler comes home.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: We keep a bell for people we hope to see again.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: There's waiting in a quiet bell.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: A bell needn't ring to remind us of someone.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Your guild keeps asking what's beyond the next hill. I keep a cup here for when you come back to tell me.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Milewardens come back with new names for faraway places. I make sure there's a seat when they tell us.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Your maps go farther than my errands. Bring me a story when you return.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The guild can keep its ink. I'll keep a cup ready for the hand that brings it home.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: You and your guildmates always want another road. I want to hear how you got back from it.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: When a Milewarden returns, we hear about country nobody here has seen. I like to be ready for that.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Welcome to {city_name}. Take a breath. The road can wait.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: First time in {city_name}? Rest your feet before you decide where to go next.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: This is {city_name}. You're welcome here. The dust on your boots can wait.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.text: We argue over who should mend a road. Then someone's child walks it, and suddenly everyone has a shovel.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Everyone has an opinion about a road until it needs mending. A child walking it usually settles the matter.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: A broken road becomes public business as soon as someone we know has to use it.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Neighbors can quarrel all morning and share a shovel before supper.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The loudest argument about a road often comes from two people who will mend it together.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper

lines.text: There's supper to set out and a traveler to fit in. That sounds right to me.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Supper is going out beside the fountain. A guest is easier to find than an excuse for an empty place.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Supper has finished. We leave the cups out to dry. Someone always remembers one more story while washing up.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The meal is over. The washing-up keeps producing more conversation.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Supper's finished, and the cups are drying. Somebody is still telling the story they started at the table.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: We cleared supper away. Nobody seems ready to clear the last story away.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The cups are washed after supper. A few neighbors linger over the drying cloths.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: Supper has ended. I leave the cups out while people finish talking.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: When the worlds came together, my family brought a kettle and the name of their village. We've replaced the kettle twice. We still use the name.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: My family's village name survived the collapse. Their kettle lasted less well. We're on the third one now.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: When the worlds joined, my family kept their village's name and brought their kettle. Two kettles later, the name remains.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: The kettle my family carried from their old world is gone. So is its replacement. We still greet people with the old village name.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: My family brought a village name and a kettle into the Endless World. The name has needed fewer repairs.

lines.speaker: fountain_keeper
lines.text: We call this place by the village name my family saved at the collapse. The kettle they brought has been replaced twice.
